title: Shell guards read PowerShell as PowerShell
when: An agent runs a command through Claude Code's PowerShell tool, or through Codex or Cursor shell tools on native Windows.
need: The guard refuses what the command does (git commit on main, writes outside the path claim, raw full-suite pytest, a foreign --session-id) exactly as it would in Bash, reading Set-Location, Remove-Item, Set-Content, Out-File and redirects. It never refuses a Bash syntax idiom PowerShell cannot have: backtick substitution, $() inside double quotes, unmatched globs, | head, 2>/dev/null, if-then status capture, sleep loops and temp-file transforms apply only to Bash. Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows is Git Bash and keeps the Bash rules.
surface: Every PreToolUse shell refusal; harness manifest shell_tools.
review: Source unit cases cover the PowerShell tokenizer, each rule's shell declaration and dispatch, the client shell stamp per harness and OS, and PowerShell path-claim targets. Live proof on a native Windows 11 machine belongs to the NATIVE-WINDOWS acceptance pass.
